text: Populist describes politics that sides with “ordinary people” against a powerful elite, often by stirring up anger. Here, attacking billionaires channels voters’ resentment of the very rich.
The vanguard is the front of a moving army, and so the leading group of any movement. Supporters of Prop 40 hope California leads the nation; opponents fear exactly that.
To nullify is to cancel the legal force of something, as if it never existed. Billionaires are funding ballot measures meant to wipe out Prop 40 if it passes.
A villain is the bad guy in a story. The writer means that every party finds it useful to point at an enemy to rally supporters.
Socialists want the government to own more of the economy or to redistribute wealth more heavily. Republicans use the word as an insult for Democrats on the left.
A billionaire owns assets worth at least a thousand million dollars. About 260 of them live in California and would pay Prop 40.
A flank is the side of an army or group. The party’s left flank means its most left-wing members.
A phrase critics use to say capitalism has grown extreme, with great inequality and corporate power. The “hopefully” hints they expect it to end.
Angst is a deep, anxious unease about the state of things.
In California, a proposition is a measure placed on the ballot for voters to decide directly, shortened to “Prop”.
A wealth tax takes a percentage of everything a person owns, not of what they earn in a year. Prop 40 would take 5% of each billionaire’s fortune, once.
A ballot measure is a law or tax that voters approve or reject directly on election day rather than through legislators.
Coherent means logical and well put together, so the parts fit. The writer says anger at billionaires is easier than designing a policy that makes sense.
Sympathy is feeling sorry for someone. Few Californians feel sorry for tech billionaires.
Barons were medieval lords with great land and power. Calling rich tech founders “barons” hints at how much power they hold.
Musing means thinking aloud in a thoughtful, wandering way, here about whether humanity will or should survive AI.
As a noun, a levy is a tax or charge imposed by authority. Fear that it would push the rich away is why it is controversial.
A state’s tax base is the people, firms and wealth it can collect taxes from. If rich people leave, the base shrinks.
Controversial means causing strong public disagreement.
Anger at elites that politicians tap into to win votes.
A story whose purpose is to warn others of what can go wrong. California’s fight may warn Democrats elsewhere.
A term-limited official may not run again after serving the maximum number of terms, so Mr Newsom must leave office.
Used figuratively, a headache is a persistent annoying problem.
A supermajority is far more than half of seats in a legislature, enough to pass laws without the other party’s help.
British spelling of skepticism: doubt about whether something is true or wise.

t: not wanting to look a sop
text: A sop is something given to appease. Here the idea is that Mr Newsom does not want to seem like a pushover who does favours for the rich.
Tinkering means making small adjustments, often in a way that falls short of real change.
The nationwide rulebook for taxes written by Congress, as opposed to taxes set by a single state.
Conspicuous means easy to see and meant to be noticed, like visits made to be seen by early-primary voters.
Primaries are elections in which a party’s voters choose their candidate for the main election. States with early primaries matter to presidential hopefuls.
An idiom meaning secretly controlled or heavily influenced by someone, usually because of money.
Donors give money to a campaign or cause, often large sums.
Infighting is quarrelling inside a group that should be united.
To degrade is to lower in quality or standing.
Bickering is petty, repeated arguing.
To cook up a plan is to invent it, often cleverly or slyly.
Bullying is using power or threats to push others around.
A deliberate effort to damage someone’s reputation with unfair accusations.
An idiom meaning to do someone else’s work or defend their interests, usually without being rewarded.
A simple majority is more than half the votes cast, so 50% plus one.
Used figuratively, toxicity means a poisonous, hostile atmosphere.
Here, fatigue means weariness. Voters tired of constant ballot measures may disengage.
Tediously means in a boring, tiring way.
A 1978 California measure capping property taxes. It is remembered for sparking a nationwide tax revolt and for distorting the housing market.
A popular movement of voters demanding lower taxes.
Distorted means twisted away from its normal shape. Prop 13 pushed housing prices and sales into odd patterns.
Senator from Vermont and leading voice of the Democratic left, a champion of taxing the rich.
Congressman for part of Silicon Valley, a progressive Democrat who backs Prop 40.
Co-founder of Google and one of the world’s richest people; he gave $102m to oppose the tax.
California’s Democratic governor, who opposes Prop 40 and is seen as a possible presidential candidate.
Head of the health-care workers’ union SEIU-UHW and the architect of Prop 40.
A Democrat expected to become California’s next governor, who is considering an income tax on the wealthy.
The 2025 federal law pushed by Donald Trump that cut taxes and, critics say, cut health-care funding.
